is filed against order dated 26.11.2024 and order dated 16.03.2023,
passed by Ld. Trial Court i.e., JMFC (Mahila Court 01), N/W Rohini, Delhi, in DV complaint case no. 3052/23, Titled Parardha Goel Vs. Rishabh Bhutoria & Ors., filed by respondent (

referred to as complainant) against appellants (herein after, referred to as R-2 & R-3).
2. TCR has been received.
Arguments heard.
3. The petition before Ld. Trial Court was filed on 16.03.2023 itself when the first impugned order was passed.
The complainant has filed the petition alleging that she was subjected to domestic violence, therefore, prayed for various reliefs under the Act.

4. Along with the petition, complainant had also filed an application for interim relief with prayers to restrain the respondents from committing further domestic violence, pass residential orders and restrain the respondents from creating third party interest in the matrimonial home i.e., H. No. 47,
Vigyan Vihar, First Floor, Near Yamuna Sports Complex.
5. The complainant had filed an application seeking prayer to direct the respondents to deposit their passport before the Court.

It was alleged in the application that the husband is permanent resident of Toronto, Canada and the complainant has filed complaint u/s 498A/ 406 IPC before CAW Cell,
however, the other respondents are planning to free from India which will affect the investigation.

sentences.text: In that application, it is stated that on 11.03.2023, the complainant came to know that the husband has already booked ticket for Canada and once he leaves India, he will never come back and the mother in law and the father in law are also in process of leaving India.

7. Therefore, Ld. Trial Court before issuing notice, on the submissions of the complainant, allowed the application and ex-parte restrained all the respondents from leaving the country without permission of Court.
8. Before Ld. Trial Court, only Respondent no
. 2 and Respondent no. 3 appeared and they filed their response.
It is stated that the husband is already residing in Canada, therefore, requested before the Court to serve the husband at Canada.
Husband has been reported to be served.

9.

Subsequently, R-2 and R-3 moved an application for modification of order dated 16.03.2023,
praying for removing the restrictions on traveling abroad.

On this application, the impugned order dated 26.11.2024 was passed whereby, Ld. Trial Court modified the order to the extent that R-2 and R-3 shall not visit any foreign country without prior intimation to the Court and their visit to foreign country shall be subject to furnishing FDR of Rs. 50,000/- each and furnishing itinerary of the visit as well as their active contact numbers or their travel and also the days of place where they would be residing.

10. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for appellant that it is not the case where the appellants are to face some charges but a DV petition only in which there are no allegations against the appellants but have been roped only because they are the parents of the husband of complainant.

It is stated that there is no relief against the appellants which can be given by the Ld. Trial Court, despite that the appellants are Digitally signed by SANJAY BHUTORIA Vs. PARARDHA GOEL CA 5-2025 PageVIKRAM 3 of page 5 VIKRAM

2025.05.05 17:20:34 +0530 subjected to such harsh conditions of furnishing not just the bonds but also their itineraries and contact details while their stay abroad.

11. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for appellants that there has been subsequent developments and now the complainant has taken ex- parte divorce from her husband, therefore, there is no domestic relation subsisting between the appellants and complainant.
Hence, all these conditions of disclosing their contact details as well as itinerary are unwarranted.

Counsel for appellant has placed reliance on judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in "Hardeep Singh Arora Vs. State of Maharashtra" wherein, it was held by Hon'ble High Court that the involvement of respondents in DV Petition is not a criminal case where the presence is required for investigation and since none of the provision of DV Act except section 31 & 33, are penal in nature, DV Act cannot be said to be penal statue and the proceedings under the DV Act do not part take character of criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh Arora Vs. State of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondents in DV Act not being offender or accused in a crime, their right to travel abroad could not be abridged solely due to filing of or pendency of proceedings under the DA Act.
13. Ld. Counsel for complainant has not disputed the divorce, copy of which is filed by Ld. Counsel for appellant on record.

Therefore, of all the reliefs claimed by the petitioner in the DV Petition,
after the decree of divorce effective from 03.03.2025, except for the relief of compensation for the loss suffered, no other relief survives in the petition.
For such reliefs to be granted where the same can be secured by attachment, the conditions imposing restrictions on the respondents/ appellants are completely unwarranted.

Therefore, the order of Ld. Trial Court, passed in application for modification, dated VIKRAM Date:
